Background (from the session that started this one):
JusPrin is an AI-piloted fork of OrcaSlicer (C++/wxWidgets, with React pages in a WebView). On 2026-10-21 Kenneth decided JusPrin needs its own Preferences window instead of showing OrcaSlicer's 75-setting dialog. That dialog stays unchanged behind a link. The design is final on the canvas. The Agent setup screens were just rebuilt with shared provider/account/tool rows, so that Preferences › Agent can use the same components; that work is being committed on `jusprin-newui`, so if your worktree doesn't have `AgentConnection.tsx` yet, ask the user or wait for it. Kenneth prefers plain-English reports. Temporary notes stay uncommitted.

Task:
Build JusPrin's own Preferences window in code, matching the "Preferences" page of the JusPrin v2 canvas (https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v). Read its boards with the Artifact tool (read action with `path`): `project/prefs-window.dc.html` is the whole window, and the `prefs-*.dc.html` boards show each section and state. The note at the top of that page records the decisions.

Scope:
- An 800-wide window with a list of sections on the left: Account, Agent, Appearance, 3D view, Projects & files, Updates.
- A small "OrcaSlicer preferences…" link at the bottom of that list, which opens `GUI_App::open_preferences()` unchanged.
- It opens over any screen: the gear on Home, "Preferences…" in the project ⋯ menu (`StatusRow.cpp`, which currently calls `open_preferences`), Ctrl+, / ⌘,, and the Agent's "Agent settings" links.
- No expert options, and nothing about Bambu Cloud.
- Every setting writes the same AppConfig keys OrcaSlicer uses. Settings with side effects must call the existing OrcaSlicer functions, never copies: language (window reload), dark mode, file associations, and graphics redraws. See the post-dialog code in `GUI_App::open_preferences`.
- The Agent and Account sections must reuse the React components in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/components/AgentConnection.tsx` (`AccountRow`, `ProviderKeys`, `ToolGroup`, `ToolRow`), so Agent setup and Preferences stay identical. Read the hand-over note at `C:\Users\guitest\AppData\Roaming\Claude\side-session-notes\local_626ee175-7819-464c-a97e-9269b2eefe7e\agent-setup-rows.md`.

Decide native versus WebView by following `agent-docs/jusprin/architecture.md` "Where logic goes". The page-first rule and reuse of those components point to a React page, with C++ owning reads and writes. Read `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md` before touching any OrcaSlicer-owned file: keep such changes small and additive. Follow "Writing UI code" in `design-system.md`. Auto-slice is not a preference. JusPrin account sign-in isn't built yet, so show it disabled the way setup does.

Done means: the window works from Prepare and Home, each setting round-trips through AppConfig, the guards and `npm test` pass, and you have checked it in the running app with an isolated `--datadir`. Commit on your branch; don't push.

Shared notes folder for this group of sessions (outside the repo; read siblings' notes there, leave hand-over notes or large findings there instead of pasting them into messages): C:\Users\guitest\AppData\Roaming\Claude\side-session-notes\local_e3c69da8-9284-46a5-abe1-6bffd29cad10

# Agent setup rows: what was built (2026-10-21, uncommitted)

Shared React rows for Agent setup and a future Preferences › Agent page live in
`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/components/AgentConnection.tsx`:

- `AccountRow({ onSignIn? })`: JusPrin account block. Without `onSignIn` the
  button is disabled (sign-in is not built). Only the signed-out state exists.
- `ProviderKeys({ heading?, setup, savedKeys, onCheck, onCancel, onRemove })`:
  intro, one `ProviderKeyRow` per provider, footnote. Owns which row's form is
  open; maps host `setup_status` / `setup_keys` onto the canvas states.
  `heading` shows "Your own API key" (Preferences lists all three ways).
- `ToolGroup({ heading?, tools, onConnect, onLookAgain })` and `ToolRow`.
  Tool rows have no "Connected · Disconnect…" state: the MCP catalog does not
  say whether a tool is connected, so that needs host data first.

Gaps against the boards, left on purpose:
- Footnote keeps "You can change this later." instead of "Change this any time
  in Preferences › Agent." because that window does not exist yet.
- "Working until restart" row shows no key hint: the host never stored that
  key, and the setup status carries no hint for it.
- A key the provider refuses while being entered stays editable with a danger
  ring (no board for this); a check that never reached the provider locks the
  key as board 4 shows.

New token `component.providerRow.fieldHeight = 32` (guarded in
`tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp`), CSS `--provider-row-field-height`.
New icon `refresh-cw.svg` copied byte-for-byte from lucide-static@1.47.0.

64-## Production integration boundaries
65-
66-### Shell host
67-
68-The shell is the JusPrin window frame around OrcaSlicer's content. Build one shell, in files this fork owns, and attach it to `MainFrame` in one small place. Decisions about what happens at startup go in a bootstrap or a shell factory that the fork owns. Do not spread environment checks through OrcaSlicer's constructors.
69-
70-The first production version may still construct OrcaSlicer's old top bar, tab panel, Sidebar, and `GUI_ObjectList` where existing OrcaSlicer behavior depends on them. Leave them out of the visible layout. Do not hide them behind a separate top-level window. Stopping them from being constructed at all is a separate project, because it changes object lifetimes.
71-
72-### Build registration
73-
74-List JusPrin's source files explicitly in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/sources.cmake`. OrcaSlicer's central `src/slic3r/CMakeLists.txt` should pull that file in with one include line that never changes. The fork should not keep adding its own files to OrcaSlicer's list.
75-
76-### Workspace boundary
77-
78-The workspace API is the typed C++ interface JusPrin uses to read and change the project. The production version should keep the ideas from the proof of concept (POC) that worked:
79-
80-- separate types for plate IDs and object IDs, so one cannot be passed where the other is expected;
81-- read-only snapshots of the project;
82-- explicit errors from commands;
83-- typed reasons that say what kind of change happened;
84-- a revision number that only goes up;
85-- subscriptions that end automatically when the object holding them is destroyed, and that can be moved but not copied.
86-
87-Before production use, the API must also:
88-
89-- say which calls must run on the GUI thread;
90-- say exactly when the revision number goes up;
91-- explicitly mark the old session's IDs invalid when a project is replaced;
92-- notice changes that did not go through the adapter (the JusPrin class that implements this API on top of OrcaSlicer);
93-- report undo and redo availability whether or not any particular widget is visible;
94-- report whether an undo or redo really changed OrcaSlicer's state;
95-- not depend on `GUI_ObjectList` for commands that change the model;
96-- offer plate selection, object import and addition, and the other commands the product needs;
97-- keep wxWidgets types and OrcaSlicer types out of its public interface.
98-
99-Sometimes the operation you need exists only inside OrcaSlicer's UI code. In that case, add the smallest possible command to the OrcaSlicer class that already does the work, and name it for what it does. Do not copy the operation into JusPrin. Do not fake clicks or key presses on hidden controls.
100-
101-### Canvas presentation
--
166:#### Where logic goes: the page first
167-
168-When the same logic could live either in C++ or in a React page, put it in the page unless there is a strong reason for C++. The page is quicker to change: Vite hot-reloads it, while a C++ change means relinking a multi-gigabyte GUI library. The page's tests run in milliseconds under Vitest. The text people read is already written in the page. The text the model reads belongs there too.
169-
170-Strong reasons for C++:
171-
172-- **It reads or changes OrcaSlicer state:** presets, the model, plates, slicing, the device list. The page never owns project state (see the constraints below).
173-- **The app has to guarantee it.** This covers what a tool accepts and refuses, which tools a session may call, and what is sent to the model provider (API keys, access codes, project data). Page code can describe a limit, but only the app can enforce one.
174-- **It has to work without a page:** the MCP server, background work, tests that run without a browser.
175-- **It needs a thread the page does not have, or has to stay alive at times when the page is not.**
176-
177-The printer panel shows how this works. The app sends the page only facts: sizes, spools, which printer a card shows, and what a change altered. The page turns those facts into all of the text:
178-
179-- The page writes the model's instructions in `AgentUI/src/printerInstructions.ts` and sends them to the app with `printer_instructions`.
180-- The page writes the panel's own text in `AgentUI/src/printerWords.ts`. That is the opening line and the note that goes with each tap. The opening line is sent with `printer_opening`. The note for a tap is sent inside that tap's payload.
181-
182-The app's part:
183-
184-- It decides which tools the model gets: the five printer tools and the four settings tools, the same list in every mode.
185-- It checks every tool call.
186-- It refuses a call that does not fit the conversation. Examples are adding a printer outside an Add conversation, changing a printer other than the one the conversation is about, and changing a setting on anything other than that printer.
187-- It refuses a turn that arrives with no instructions. The app has no prompt of its own to fall back on.
188-- It posts the opening line once per session.
189-- It posts the note for a tap only when the tap goes through, and limits the note to 2 KB.
190-- It still writes the notes for things only the app can find out when the tap arrives: the network printer has gone, the printer's model id is not on the list, or a save or an undo failed.
191-
192-The project assistant works the same way. Its whole system prompt is written in `AgentUI/src/projectInstructions.ts`, and `projectInstructions.test.ts` pins it to a fixture so that a change to it is always deliberate. The page sends it with `project_instructions` on every connection. The app keeps it in the project session's profile and sends it, unchanged, as the instructions of every project request; the provider's prompt cache depends on the text staying byte-identical. The app has no default text. A turn the app starts itself before the page has sent the prompt (the first message after a file opens, or Ask AI on a print issue, while the page is still loading) waits in the reply queue and starts when the prompt arrives. The prompt lived in C++ until 2026-10-14 so that the MCP server's instructions could share part of it; they stopped sharing it on 2026-10-10. The MCP server's own instructions (`Mcp/McpProtocol.cpp`) and the request that names a conversation stay in C++: MCP has no page, and the title request is the app's own.
193-
194-Windows uses WebView2, macOS uses WKWebView, and Linux uses WebKitGTK. The way the page's files are packaged must work on all three. The prototype packed the whole page into a single local file, because WKWebView failed to load additional files referenced through `file:` URLs. Production keeps the single-file approach, and CMake now builds that file from the TypeScript/React sources.
195-
196-MCP (Model Context Protocol, which lets external AI tools call the app) and wider agent autonomy are layers that come after this one. They must go through the same typed workspace interface. They must not change who owns the 3D view.
197-
198-### Gizmo presentation
199-
200-Start with Move or Rotate. Build one reusable native controller that wraps the existing behavior:
201-
202-1. Show a compact strip of tool buttons in the upper-left corner of the Prepare canvas. The strip is a horizontal row like OrcaSlicer's own toolbar, but aligned to the left instead of centred. The strip stays put when the selection or the camera moves, because a strip attached to the object would jump every time the view orbits. `Canvas/ViewportToolStrip` draws the strip with ImGui as part of the canvas's own frame, through `GLCanvas3D::set_overlay_renderer`. On every frame it asks the gizmo manager which tool is open. The open tool's values appear below the row in `Canvas/ToolValuePanel`, lined up with the button that opened the tool.
203-2. Activate the existing native gizmo.

# Fork stewardship

**Status:** Required discipline for every change to an upstream-owned file on `jusprin-newui`.

JusPrin is a long-lived fork. Every line it changes in an OrcaSlicer-owned file is a line it re-resolves at every rebase, forever, by a person who was not there when the line was written. The rules below exist to keep that permanent cost small and, where it cannot be small, to keep it visible.

One question generates all of them: **after this change, what does the fork own?**

- Owning *product policy* is safe. It is ours, upstream will never write it, and it lives in our files.
- Owning a *small neutral seam* is acceptable. It is the kind of thing upstream might plausibly have written itself, so it survives refactors and could be contributed back.
- Owning *upstream's behavior* is the expensive kind. It commits us to re-deriving upstream's intent forever, and the day we take ownership is usually the day the behavior quietly diverges.

Two mechanical facts drive everything else. Git merges text, not meaning: it conflicts when two sides touch the same or adjacent lines, and it stays silent when they touch different lines even if the result is nonsense. And a conflict is a *stop* — a human is forced to look — while silent divergence is unbounded and invisible. Conflicts are therefore not the enemy. Unnoticed drift is, and conflicts that resolve wrongly are.

## The ten principles

### 1. Conflict probability is about where you write, not how much

**Rule.** Place fork edits where upstream rarely writes, and keep the number of distinct sites low.

**Mechanism.** Risk is roughly *how often upstream edits this region* times *how much of the region you occupy*, summed over every place you touched. Each site is an independent draw. New files have probability zero, so their size is free; one line inside a function upstream is actively reworking is expensive.

**The test.** How many separate places does this change touch, and how busy is each one? Would one seam deliver the same capability?

**Violation.** Delivering a single capability through a dozen scattered notification lines across several upstream files, when one funnel that every path already passes through would have carried them.

### 2. A clean merge is not a safe merge

**Rule.** Prefer edits that are locally correct over edits that participate in upstream's control flow.

**Mechanism.** Git merges text. If your edit's correctness depends on the code around it — an ordering, a guard, an early return, an invariant nobody wrote down — upstream can restructure the surroundings, the merge succeeds, and your edit now runs under assumptions that no longer hold, with no signal at all.

**The test.** If upstream restructures the code around this hunk, do I get a conflict or silence? If silence, would any test catch it?

**Violation.** Moving a member out of a constructor's initializer list because a callback can fire mid-construction. Nothing in upstream's code records that invariant, so a future cleanup restores the old form with no conflict and no error.

### 3. Add to upstream's code; do not revise it

**Rule.** Append, insert, and call. Do not rewrite upstream functions or change their signatures.

**Mechanism.** An additive hook fails gracefully: when it conflicts, the resolution is "keep both," and anyone can do that correctly. A rewritten function fails badly: every future upstream change to it is a conflict whose resolution requires re-deriving two intents at once, in code no longer shared with upstream. Rewriting subtle logic also tends to change it, and you find out later.

**The test.** Does upstream's line survive my change? If I deleted or replaced one, why could I not have added next to it?

**Violation.** Replacing OrcaSlicer's undo and redo implementations with fork-owned equivalents in order to learn whether the history position moved. Re-expressing the vendor-specific snapshot walk silently dropped one of its branches. An additive helper that reports the result, leaving upstream's functions untouched, would have answered the same question.

### 4. Own the policy; borrow the mechanism

**Rule.** No product name, color, dimension, or product-specific decision in an upstream-owned file. Upstream files may gain small neutral capabilities; the policy that uses them lives in fork-owned code.

**Mechanism.** Product specifics in upstream files are permanent divergence: they can never be upstreamed and never dropped, so they must be re-resolved forever. A neutral capability — a flag, a getter/setter pair, an event — reads like something upstream could have written, which is exactly why it survives refactors.

**The test.** Would this addition look reasonable in an upstream pull request, with no explanation of our product?

**Violation.** A product-named enum value inside a rendering class, or product decisions embedded in an upstream mouse handler. The fix is a neutral options struct plus a fork-owned controller that applies our policy.

### 5. One seam beats many touch points

**Rule.** Find the single place every path already passes through, and put the fork's line there.

**Mechanism.** Each touch point is an independent conflict draw and an independent thing a future resolver must understand. Collapsing many small recurring costs into one is worth some indirection.

**The test.** Do all the paths I am hooking already converge somewhere downstream? Is there one function that runs exactly when the thing I care about has happened?

**Violation.** Publishing a history-changed event from undo, from redo, and from both history-navigation entry points, when all four funnel through a single update function that runs only on a successful move.

### 6. One shared implementation is worth a guaranteed conflict

**Rule.** When the alternative is two copies of the same behavior, keep the shared path and accept that it will conflict.

**Mechanism.** A conflict is a stop; drift between two copies is silent and unbounded. Trading an invisible risk for a visible, small, recurring one is a good trade.

**The test.** Where did the logic I removed actually go? A move has one implementation; only a duplication risks divergence. If I wrote new behavior beside an existing upstream path rather than calling it, upstream's future improvements will never reach our users.

**Violation.** Writing a second object-duplication routine next to OrcaSlicer's clipboard path and pointing an existing dialog at it. Reusing the existing path — extending it where it was too narrow — keeps one implementation.

### 7. Unavoidable conflicts must be easy to resolve correctly

**Rule.** When you must delete or relocate an upstream line, say at the site what moved, where it went, and what a future rebase must carry across.

**Mechanism.** The real cost of a conflict is not the stop; it is the chance of resolving it wrongly. Appending near an upstream line yields a conflict whose obvious resolution — keep both — is right. Deleting an upstream line yields a conflict whose obvious resolution — take mine, the logic moved — silently discards whatever upstream did to that line in the meantime.

**The test.** Six months from now, is the natural resolution of the conflict I am creating the correct one? If not, what does the resolver need to read to get it right, and is that text next to the conflict?

**Violation.** Removing an upstream snapshot label that upstream later localized. Git stops for a human, but the intent-faithful resolution throws the translation away, and nothing at the site says otherwise.

### 8. Do not diverge where you gain nothing; converge where upstream already went

**Rule.** No gratuitous formatting, reordering, or whitespace differences. Before reverting a cosmetic difference, compare against current upstream — it may have made the same change.

**Mechanism.** Every valueless difference is a conflict site that buys nothing. And if upstream has independently arrived at your version, "fixing" it back creates divergence rather than removing it. Adopting a change upstream has already made converges the two trees early and makes the eventual conflict resolve itself.

**The test.** Does this difference carry meaning? Has upstream already made it?

**Violation.** Consuming a shared blank line in a list of build subdirectories, where upstream also appends entries.

### 9. Verify the risk claim instead of reasoning about it

**Rule.** Before asserting that a change is or is not rebase-risky, check it. Three checks, each one command: does git actually conflict there; has upstream already converged on the same change; is the change a move or a duplication.

**Mechanism.** A coherent story about fork risk is not a true one, and every one of these is cheaper to check than to argue about. Reasoning alone reliably produces confident, wrong claims — that a lost change is "silent" when git stops for it, that a move is a "duplication," that a cosmetic difference is gratuitous when upstream shares it.

**The test.** Did I run the simulation, or am I describing what I expect it to say?

**Violation.** A report that lists which files are rebase-sensitive and calls the change narrow, without having run the merge simulation that would have found two lossy resolutions waiting in it.

### 10. Pull direction dominates every local edit

**Rule.** Replay the fork's own commits onto upstream. Never merge upstream in, and never rebase the whole branch.

**Mechanism.** The fork's own footprint is small; the inherited release-branch history is not. Merging upstream in makes the conflict surface the entire divergence between the release branch and upstream's development line — none of it ours. Rebasing only our commits discards that inherited history by taking upstream's version of every file we never touched.

**The test.** Am I replaying our commits onto upstream, or bringing upstream into ours?

**Violation.** `git merge upstream/main`, which produces a conflict list dominated by vendor profiles, translations, and CI files that JusPrin has never edited.

## Before you finish

A change that touches upstream-owned files is not done until this is recorded in the handback or pull request:

173:## Writing UI code
174-
175-Rules for anyone, human or agent, adding or changing a JusPrin surface. They
176-exist because every value that is typed by hand drifts from the design system and
177-from the other side of the app within weeks; today's guards catch most of it, but
178-only if the code goes through the token file in the first place.
179-
180-1. **Never type a color, radius, font, or control size.** Every one comes
181-   from `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`. Native code reads it
182-   through `ShellTheme`: `palette(dark)` for color, `metrics()` for radii,
183-   spacing, and per-component sizes, `font(role)` for type. A stock
184-   `wxStaticText`, `wxTextCtrl`, or OrcaSlicer `Button` is
185-   dressed through `Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp`, never by calling its setters
186-   with literals. The Agent page uses only `var(--…)`: `--<group>-<name>` for
187-   color, `--radius-<name>`, `--font-<role>`, `--font-code`, and
188-   `--button-<recipe>-padding`.
189-2. **If the value you need has no token, add the token first.** Put it in
190-   the JSON, extend the guard in `tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp` so a
191-   later edit cannot silently move it, then read it from code. Do not write
192-   the number "for now": the guards cannot see a literal that is already
193-   there, and the next reader cannot tell a decision from an accident. A
194-   value that exists in the design artifacts but not in the roles or scales is a design
195-   decision to raise, not a reason to type it.
196-3. **Layout spacing may stay literal, on the scale.** Padding between
197-   regions, gaps, and margins use 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, or 48 DIP.
198-   Control padding is not layout spacing; it comes from a button recipe.
199-4. **Pick the nearest role, never a bespoke size.** The roles are the whole
200-   type system. Bold at a body or label size is a role of its own; if a
201-   surface seems to need a size that no role has, see rule 2.
202-5. **The design system wins when it and the code disagree.** The two Claude

import { StrictMode } from 'react';
import { createRoot } from 'react-dom/client';
import { App } from './App';
import { nativeTransport } from './bridge/client';
import { applyAppearance, applyStaticTokens } from './tokens';
import './styles.css';

applyStaticTokens();
applyAppearance('light');

// A throwaway, setup-only host (e.g. embedded in the Add a printer dialog)
// loads this same page with ?embedded=1 so it renders only the setup
// sub-component instead of the full conversation chrome. See App.tsx.
const query = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search);
const embedded = query.get('embedded') === '1';
// The temporary printer task chat loads the same page with ?panel=printer: the same
// thread and composer, with the printer session's card pinned above them
// instead of the project's setup card. See App.tsx.
const panel = query.get('panel') === 'printer';

createRoot(document.getElementById('root')!).render(
  <StrictMode>
    <App getTransport={nativeTransport} embedded={embedded} printerPanel={panel} />
  </StrictMode>,
);

The JusPrin Windows verification box (Windows Server 2022, user `guitest`, as of 2026-09-09): no admin rights, no GPU, reached over RDP at 100% scaling. VS 2022 Build Tools, CMake and Ninja are installed; the deps live at `C:/src/JusPrin/deps/build/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local`. Main checkout `C:/src/JusPrin` is on `jusprin-newui` with a Release build in `C:/src/JusPrin/build`.

**Why:** Several handoff items were blocked on machine facts (no debugger, no admin, DPI cannot change from inside an RDP session), so knowing them up front saves a diagnostic pass.

**How to apply:**
- GL needs Mesa, and **every freshly configured CMake build tree starts without it** — nothing in CMake or the repo supplies it. Run `pwsh src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/windows-gl/provision-mesa-windows.ps1 -BuildDir <build dir> -Source C:\src\JusPrin\build\src\Release` after configuring; it copies `libgallium_wgl.dll` and `dxil.dll` (from `C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10\Redist\D3D\x64\`) beside every GUI exe and `opengl32.dll` into its `mesa\` subfolder. Placement is not interchangeable, and each missing file has a silent signature — both documented in "Software GL on Windows machines without a GPU" in `agent-docs/jusprin/engineering-method.md` (on `jusprin-newui` since 2026-09-13, commit `318208608f`).
- Quick recall of the signatures: no `libgallium_wgl.dll` → `glcontext not ready, postpone init`, no `got opengl version`, black canvas all session. No `dxil.dll` → d3d12 initializes, then exit `0x80070057` on the first canvas draw with nothing logged. Both verified by removing the file and re-running. With all three present, both `d3d12` (default, `4.2 … D3D12`) and `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` (`4.6 … llvmpipe`) render.
- `slow_bootup` only moves the dxil crash from startup to first canvas paint; it is not a workaround.
- Lesson: a clear-only WGL smoke test passed under d3d12 because clearing compiles no shader, and was wrongly read as clearing the driver. A smoke test that skips the suspect code path proves nothing about it. (That test was removed from the repo for this reason.)
- A first-run datadir (e.g. copies of `C:\b\dd3`) logs ~630k lines in the first minute — the `GuideFrame::GetFilamentInfo` profile scan, driver-independent. Not a GL symptom.
- `D3D12 (Microsoft Basic Render Driver)` in the log is **Mesa's own d3d12 gallium driver on WARP**, not Microsoft's GLon12 mapping layer and not a real GPU. Confirm which GL is live by listing the process's loaded modules: the bundled Mesa shows `<exe dir>\mesa\opengl32.dll` + `libgallium_wgl.dll` (+ `DXIL.dll` once d3d12 has drawn), the unprovisioned fallback shows only `C:\Windows\SYSTEM32\OPENGL32.dll`.
- The permission guard refuses `Remove-Item` under `C:\b` (it reports it as a protected path) and misparses `rd /s /q` and path-like string literals as delete targets. Hand build-tree deletion to the user; build trees there contain `resources` symlinks into live worktrees, so unlink those before any recursive delete.
- A debugger can be had without admin: download `https://aka.ms/windbg/download` (an .appinstaller pointing at a ~1.2 GB msixbundle), unzip the bundle, unzip `windbg_win-x64.msix`, and `amd64/cdb.exe` runs directly. Set `_NO_DEBUG_HEAP=1` when running the harness under cdb, or teardown crawls in the debug heap for many minutes.
- Fixture directories for the harness's visual modes must be short paths (e.g. `C:\Users\guitest\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\wp\...`); a long scratchpad path makes the profile-bundle copy exceed MAX_PATH and the fixture slice never validates.
- The harness prints everything on stderr; the exit code must be read with `$LASTEXITCODE` in PowerShell (bash shows 127).
- DPI at 150%/200% needs the user to reconnect the RDP session at that scale. See [[jusprin-windows-parity-handoff]].

Node is installed twice: the older `C:\tools\node` (v24.20.0), which is **not on PATH**, and
`C:\Users\guitest\.local\node-v24.21.0-win-x64` (v24.21.0, npm 11.19.0), added to the **user
PATH** on 2026-09-16. Check `Get-Command npm.cmd` before installing anything; a fresh Bash
session may still need `export PATH="$PATH:/c/Users/guitest/.local/node-v24.21.0-win-x64"`.

npm is not optional any more: since commit `5fc0efe2e3` the Agent and Home pages are built from
TypeScript and their `resources/jusprin/{agent,home}/index.html` is generated, not committed.
Without npm, CMake **fails at configure time** (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Web/CMakeLists.txt`
`FATAL_ERROR`), so the first new source file you add breaks the build tree; and without the
bundles the app creates no Agent WebView at all, which shows up as `shell_agent_webview_created
FAIL` / "the Agent page did not complete its handshake" in the shell harness. Build them with
`npm ci && npm run build` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI` and `HomeUI`.

The shell harness and the Agent page must come from the same commit: a harness exe built before
a page change hangs at `agent_reply_streams_to_completion` instead of failing.

To work on `jusprin-mcp` (the MCP stdio helper) you do **not** need an app build, and a worktree
can have its own build tree in about three minutes: configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF`
(skips the npm requirement above) plus
`-DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=C:/src/JusPrin/deps/build/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local`, then
`cmake --build <dir> --config Release --target jusprin-mcp -- -m`, which compiles only the six
bridge/registry sources and `main.cpp`. `vswhere.exe` is **not** installed; vcvars is at
`C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft Visual Studio\2022\BuildTools\VC\Auxiliary\Build\vcvars64.bat`
and cmake at `C:\tools\cmake\bin\cmake.exe`. Point the Python suite at the result with
`JUSPRIN_TEST_BRIDGE=<dir>\src\Release\jusprin-mcp.exe`; the whole suite runs in ~8 s.

An **existing** build tree configured before node was installed keeps `JUSPRIN_NPM:FILEPATH=JUSPRIN_NPM-NOTFOUND`
in its CMakeCache, and `find_program` never retries a cached NOTFOUND -- so the next build fails at
configure with the `npm not found` FATAL_ERROR even once npm is on PATH. Reconfigure the tree once with
`cmake . -DJUSPRIN_NPM="C:/Users/guitest/.local/node-v24.21.0-win-x64/npm.cmd"`; putting node on PATH alone
is not enough. Neither the Bash tool nor a PowerShell session started before 2026-09-16 inherits the user
PATH entry, so prefix `$env:PATH` explicitly in each invocation.

**Shared build tree (2026-09-17):** other Claude sessions build and commit from `C:\src\JusPrin` and
`C:\src\JusPrin\build` concurrently. Do not patch that checkout or build there from a worktree session;
a link there holds `.lib` files and breaks their build (LNK1104). Use a separate tree instead: configure
with `-DBUILD_TESTS=ON -DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF -DSLIC3R_MSVC_PDB=OFF -DDEP_BUILD_DIR=C:/src/JusPrin/deps/build`
at a short path such as `C:\b\wsh`, which is a full `libslic3r_gui` build of about 40 minutes. To symbolize a crash
without a debugger, relink with a `ForceImportAfterCppTargets` props file (Link `GenerateDebugInformation`/`GenerateMapFile`),
read the fault offset from the event log (Application, event 1000), and run
`llvm-symbolizer --obj=<exe> --relative-address <offset>` (the symbolizer ships in the MSVC bin dir).

- The in-app browser pane renders a `file://` page as a static snapshot and refuses `screenshot`.
  To look at a rendered page (e.g. a vitest `PREVIEW_OUT` page), serve the directory over a
  throwaway node http server on 127.0.0.1 and navigate to that instead.

**Commits can hang in the `entire` hook (2026-09-25):** `git commit` from an agent session in a worktree
never returned; `entire hooks git prepare-commit-msg <file> message` alone hangs too (60 s, no output,
stdin closed). `--no-verify` does not skip prepare-commit-msg, and hooks must not be bypassed anyway, so
stop after one timed attempt (`timeout 90 git commit ... < /dev/null`), kill the orphaned `entire`
process it leaves behind (`ps -W | grep entire`), and ask Kenneth. Other sessions' commits carry an
`Entire-Checkpoint` trailer, so the hook works somewhere; the cause was not found.

**Concurrent harness runs collide on WebView2 (2026-09-25):** every harness exe uses the same WebView2
profile, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\JusPrin2\EBWebView`. While another session's harness is running (e.g. a
long `--home-printers-live` fixture run), a second harness fails at once with
`shell_agent_page_handshake_complete FAIL`, and its app log shows `JusPrin agent page failed to load:
The group or resource is not in the correct state`. That is not a page or bundle problem. Check for
`shell_integration_harness.exe` in `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process`, don't kill another session's
process, and set `$env:WEBVIEW2_USER_DATA_FOLDER='C:\b\<tree>-webview'` for your own runs.

**Scripting on this box (2026-10-06):** there is no `python`/`py`; use node (`C:\Users\guitest\.local\node-v24.21.0-win-x64`). Bash heredocs and `node -e "..."` that contain backticks, `${...}` or backslashes get mangled by the shell; write the script to a file with the Write tool and run `node <file>`. The main checkout's build tree `C:\src\JusPrin\build` (VS generator, Release) is fine to build from a session that is working in the main checkout: `cmake --build C:\src\JusPrin\build --config Release --target <targets> -- -m` after `vcvars64.bat`; harness exes there read `resources\` from the source tree, so `npm run build` in `AgentUI` is enough to refresh the Agent page. A touched `Workspace.hpp` rebuild of `libslic3r_gui` + `shell_integration_harness` takes roughly 10 minutes.

name: verify-the-basic-path-in-the-app
description: "On JusPrin UI work, exercise the screen's primary click path in the running app and validate the capture method first; unit tests and static screenshots hid basic defects."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory

---

On the Home screen (2026-09-12) I shipped a review-ready branch after passing every
guard, then the user immediately found two things I never tried: the Agent chat panel
was still on screen, and clicking a project card led nowhere useful. Both were one
click away.

**Why:** I checked the *page* against the mockup instead of the *screen*, and I stopped
at "synthetic input is blocked on this machine" instead of finding another way in.
Worse, my capture method was `PrintWindow`, which renders OpenGL content black **and
omits modal dialogs entirely** — so my "verification" screenshots were structurally
blind to exactly the defects that were there. I verified with an instrument I never
validated.

**How to apply:**
- Before trusting a screenshot, prove the capture shows what is really on screen.
  `PrintWindow` lies about GL and modals; `CopyFromScreen` of the window rect does not.
- Drive the page's own controls over the WebView2 DevTools protocol when the OS refuses
  synthetic input: launch with `REDACTED`,
  then `Runtime.evaluate` a real `element.click()` on the target. See
  [[windows-ui-testing-without-a-desktop]]. That click goes through the real handler and
  the real bridge, and it found two more defects the guards could not.
- Run the screen's primary gesture end to end in the app before calling UI work done,
  and compare the whole window against the design, not just the surface you wrote.
- Config levers that remove blockers without clicking: `default_page=1` lands on the
  editor, `no_warn_when_modified_gcodes=true` suppresses the customized-preset modal,
  `backup_switch=false` stops the restore prompt.

name: entire-commit-hook-hangs
description: "git commit hangs in Entire's prepare-commit-msg on Windows because Entire opens CONIN$ for a [Y/n] link prompt; GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 makes it non-interactive"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 673eb384-7139-489f-8ef7-aa76f6ab7efa
  modified: 2026-09-27T05:53:11.186Z
---

Root cause (diagnosed 2026-09-25, Entire CLI 0.11.0): when the committing session has file changes to link,
`entire hooks git prepare-commit-msg <file> message` shows "Link this commit to session context? [Y/n]" and reads the
answer from `CONIN$`, not stdin. The agent's Git Bash has a hidden console, so the open succeeds and the read blocks forever.
`</dev/null` does not help. Commits with nothing to link skip the prompt, which is why it looked intermittent.
The log is buffered, so `.entire/logs/entire.log` shows nothing until the process exits.
Evidence: handle dump of the hung process showed a `\Device\ConDrv` handle with a blocked synchronous read.
Entire's own Pi integration prefixes agent bash commands with `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` for this exact reason.
With `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` the same hook finished in ~0.3s and added the trailer, 3 of 3 runs; without it, 3 of 3 hung.

**Why:** It looks like a slow checkpoint condense, so it is easy to wait a long time for nothing.
A separate, real slowdown also exists: an `msbuild -m` build pins all 16 cores (processor queue ~64) and every
`entire` launch then takes 5-20s. That is slow, not hung; don't confuse the two.

**How to apply:** Fixed 2026-09-25: `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` is set as a user env var (HKCU\Environment), so Claude and Codex
shells inherit it after the app restarts (verified in Claude: 3/3 hook runs 0.3s with trailer). If a commit hangs again, first check
`echo $GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT` in the agent shell. Restarting the Claude app: the tray has no Quit, so end all `claude` processes
from a helper launched via WMI (outside Claude's tree) and relaunch with `explorer.exe shell:AppsFolder\Claude_pzs8sxrjxfjjc!Claude`.
If one hangs anyway, kill only that commit's `entire` PID; never `--no-verify`. See [[windows-build-machine]].

2026-09-27: with `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` already set, a `git merge --no-ff` (merge commit) in a worktree still ran past a
120 s `timeout` -- but the merge commit was already written correctly and nothing was left running. After a timeout, check
`git log -1` and the parents before retrying; a retry would make a second commit. A plain `git commit` minutes earlier took ~seconds.

See `orca-integration-guide.md` section 3.

| Message family in my check | What it usually means |
| --- | --- |
| Layer height or a line width against the nozzle (\"Layer height cannot exceed nozzle diameter\", \"Too large line width\") | A process setting does not fit the selected nozzle; the setting key names which. |
| \"Plate N: <plate type> is not suggested for use printing filament N (<filament>)\" | That filament's preset has no bed temperature for this plate type; no setting is named. A different plate type or a different filament fixes it; the bed temperature the message offers instead prints a material on a surface its maker does not recommend. |
| An object that exceeds the build volume or its height, or collides with another when printed one by one | Size, position or print order; the object is named. Scaling changes the object the person wanted. |
| Organic or tree support diameters, support base patterns, support enforcers with support off | Support settings that contradict each other or are missing; the key names the one to change. |
| Prime tower requirements, an extruder the printer does not have, nozzles of different diameters | Multi-material or multi-extruder settings that disagree across objects or with the printer. |
| Spiral vase with more than one material, a smooth timelapse or clumping detection with the \"by object\" sequence | Two modes that cannot run together; one has to go, and which is the person's choice when it changes what they asked for. |
| Speed, acceleration or jerk above the printer's maximum; precise Z height or clumping detection beside the prime tower | Warnings, not refusals: I slice anyway, capping the motion values. |"

# JusPrin Preferences window: what was built (2026-10-21)

Branch `claude/musing-wing-e808a9` (worktree `musing-wing-e808a9`), on top of
`jusprin-newui` 6570f42a00 (the Agent setup rows commit). Build tree `C:\b\prf`
(`C:\b\prf-build.cmd <targets>`).

## Shape

- The window is the Agent page in a fourth mode, `?panel=preferences`
  (`AgentPageMode::Preferences`), so Agent and Account reuse `AccountRow`,
  `ProviderKeys`, `ToolGroup` and the tool-connect flow (`SetupLocalTool`, which
  gained `startTool`) unchanged.
- Native: `JusPrin/Preferences/PreferencesWindow.{hpp,cpp}` (modal wxDialog,
  in-memory ProjectPersistence like the printer panel, its own AgentHost that
  shares the docked host's MCP helper settings) and
  `PreferencesSettings.{hpp,cpp}` (GUI-free: reads/writes AppConfig with the
  exact keys and values OrcaSlicer's dialog writes; unit-tested in
  `jusprin_profile_tests`).
- Protocol: page `preferences_action` ({action:"set",name,value} or a command),
  host `preferences` (full snapshot after every change; also the `state`
  session on hello). Capability `preferences`.
- Entry points: `GUI_App::set_preferences_handler` (new hook at the top of
  `open_preferences`) routes every OrcaSlicer entry (menus, Ctrl+P, macOS
  Cmd+,, StatusRow's ⋯ "Preferences…") to the window; Ctrl+, from the frame's
  CHAR_HOOK, from the Agent page and from Home's page; Home gets a gear at the
  top of the printer column; "Configure Agent" (connected agent) opens it on
  Agent. A request for an OrcaSlicer tab/option (hints) still gets OrcaSlicer's
  dialog. The window's "OrcaSlicer preferences…" link closes it, then calls
  `open_preferences()` with the hook bypassed.

## Upstream edits (fork-owned files aside)

- `GUI_App.hpp/.cpp`: the handler hook; `apply_language()` and
  `apply_dark_mode_setting()` moved out of `open_preferences` and the dialog's
  dark-mode lambda (both callers now share them); `online_version()` read
  accessor for the private `version_info`.
- `Preferences.hpp/.cpp`: the language list and names moved into static
  `offered_languages()` / `language_name()`; the dark-mode lambda calls
  `apply_dark_mode_setting()`.

## Left out on purpose

- "New chats start with" Model/Thinking rows: the app stores no default model
  or thinking level for new chats (only a default provider), so building it
  means changing how chats start. Needs a decision.
- Updates shows the version and "Check now" (OrcaSlicer's own check, which
  reports in its own dialog); no "Up to date · checked [time]" line, because
  nothing records when the last check ran or that it found nothing.
- The canvas title row with its own close button: the window uses the native
  title bar ("Preferences" + close) instead.

---
name: crash-stacks-without-a-debugger
description: "Get a symbolized call stack for a native crash on the Windows box in minutes: C:\\b\\minidbg (Win32 debug API) plus a build tree compiled with /Z7 and linked /DEBUG; traps that cost a full rebuild"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: c04fbdd1-d707-42dc-922c-7911bb1d35e0
  modified: 2026-10-14T17:09:52.100Z

`C:\b\minidbg\minidbg.exe <exe> [args]` (source `minidbg.cpp` beside it, built with `cl /std:c++17 /EHsc /DUNICODE`) runs a program under the Win32 debug API and prints a symbolized stack, with file:line where a PDB exists, for every access violation, heap corruption, stack-buffer overrun and second-chance exception. No WinDbg download needed. Set `_NO_DEBUG_HEAP=1`. `run-harness-example.ps1` there shows the env setup for the shell harness. Used 2026-10-14 to find the Check Print crash: the stack led straight to `GCodeViewer::init` → `strlen(glGetString(GL_VERSION))` with no current GL context.

For line numbers you need a tree with debug info. Configure with
`"-DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS_RELEASE=/MD /O2 /Ob2 /DNDEBUG /Z7"`, the same for C, and `"-DCMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS_RELEASE=/DEBUG:FULL /OPT:REF /OPT:ICF"` (example: `C:\b\ckp-build.cmd`). **Keep `/MD`.** Overriding the flags without it compiles everything `/MT`, and the link fails only at the very end with `LNK2038 RuntimeLibrary mismatch` against opencv/libcurl, after a 40-minute build. `SLIC3R_MSVC_PDB` is declared in CMakeLists.txt but nothing reads it.

Quick triage without any of this: the event-log fault offset in a system DLL maps to a function via `dumpbin /exports <dll>` (the nearest export at or below the offset). ucrtbase `0x2a341` is `strlen+0x31`, meaning a null or bad `char*`.

Run harnesses with `Start-Process -RedirectStandardError` rather than PowerShell `2>`. A PowerShell native-command redirect writes the file only when the process exits, so a hung run shows a 0-byte log. Visible windows of a stuck process can be listed with `C:\b\ckp-windows.ps1 -ProcessId <pid>` (a `#32770` titled 引导_P21 is OrcaSlicer's setup guide left open).

Windows GL fact found the same day: `wxGLCanvas::Create` on MSW always ends with `wglMakeCurrent(nullptr, nullptr)`. Creating any GL canvas leaves no context current, so GL work right after constructing a canvas needs an explicit make-current first. Upstream's helper for this is `GLCanvas3D::_set_shown_canvas_current`.

See [[windows-build-machine]].

I've built JusPrin's own Preferences window and committed it as `fa46fb1bd4` on `claude/musing-wing-e808a9` (not pushed). It works in the running app. The one thing that doesn't work well is a language change, which ends with a broken Agent panel and once crashed the app.

**What you get**
- An 800×640 window with the six sections in a list on the left, and "OrcaSlicer preferences…" at the bottom. That link closes the window and opens OrcaSlicer's own dialog unchanged.
- It's a React page: the Agent page bundle loaded in a fourth mode. Account and Agent use the same `AccountRow`, `ProviderKeys`, `ToolGroup` and tool-connect screens as Agent setup. Account sign-in shows disabled, as setup does.
- C++ does all reading and writing. Every setting uses the AppConfig key and value OrcaSlicer's dialog writes. Side effects call OrcaSlicer's own functions: file and link associations, the update check, the dark-mode switch, the language switch and window reload.
- Ways in:
  - the ⋯ "Preferences…" menu in a project, which now shows its shortcut;
  - Ctrl+, from the main window, the Agent panel and Home (⌘, on macOS);
  - a new gear on Home, at the top of the printers column;
  - "Configure Agent" once an agent is set up;
  - every OrcaSlicer route into Preferences. OrcaSlicer hints that point at one of its own options still open its dialog.
- Setup's footnote now says "Change this any time in Preferences › Agent."

**Changes to OrcaSlicer's files**
- `GUI_App`: a hook at the top of `open_preferences()`, and a read accessor for the found update version.
- Code moved out so the old dialog and the new window share one copy: the language switch, the dark-mode switch, and the language list with its names.

I also added a `component.preferences` size token (with its guard) and five icons copied from the pinned Lucide package.

**Checks**
- `npm test` and the type check pass for the Agent page, except four tests (plus timeouts) that fail on this machine because files are checked out with Windows line endings. The new Preferences tests and the Home tests all pass.
- `brand_tokens_tests`, `shell_theme_tests`, `jusprin_tests` and the new AppConfig round-trip tests pass.
- `agent_bridge_tests` has one failure, the same line-ending cause.
- In the app, with its own `--datadir`:
  - opened it from Home's gear and from Prepare;
  - changed settings and confirmed each value landed in the config file exactly as OrcaSlicer writes it;
  - OrcaSlicer's dialog then showed the same values;
  - dark mode applied everywhere.

Two problems turned up there and are fixed: checkbox rows were centred, and switching theme jumped back to Account.

**Not built**
- "New chats start with" model and thinking: the app stores no default model for new chats. Adding one changes how chats start, so it needs your decision.
- The Updates "checked [time]" line: nothing records when the last check ran. The section shows the version and "Check now", which runs OrcaSlicer's own check and reports in its own dialog.
- The window uses the system title bar instead of the canvas's own title row and close button.

**Language change, the open problem**
I tested it three times. This machine has no Python, so it builds no translation files; I copied in a German one by hand for the test and removed it afterwards. The language is saved, and the rebuilt window shows it with the project still open. But every time, the Agent panel then reads "The Agent panel could not connect". Once, starting from Prepare, the app crashed while closing the old window, and that didn't happen again in two later runs. The reload is OrcaSlicer's own window rebuild, the same call its dialog makes, and nothing had tested it with the JusPrin shell before. So it is probably not caused by the new window, but I haven't proven that.

content.text:
I've found and fixed the real cause of the language-change failure, and worked through Kenneth's other four points. Two new commits on `claude/musing-wing-e808a9`, not pushed: `01e38797cd` (the language fix) and `95ab4ea1c2` (the Preferences rework).

**5. Language change: cause found and fixed.**
- **Cause:** every embedded web page runs inside an Edge "environment", and wx sets that environment's language to the app's current language. Edge refuses to start a new environment whose settings differ from the browser process already running on the same data folder, and the error it gives is exactly "The group or resource is not in the correct state". OrcaSlicer's window reload builds the new window while the old one, and its browser process with the old language, is still alive. So after a language change, every new page was refused.
- **Evidence:** before the switch, the running browser process had `--lang=de-DE`. Asking for English failed with that exact error, even though no browser process was left once the old window closed.
- **Fix:** every environment in a run now uses the language the first page started with. No page reads that value: JusPrin's pages take no language from it, and OrcaSlicer's pages get theirs another way.
- **Result:** three switches in one run (German, English, German). The Agent panel and Home reconnected every time, and the app stayed up.
- **The crash:** it happened once in three runs before the fix, and hasn't happened since. I think it came from the failed pages being torn down, but I haven't proven that.
- OrcaSlicer's own language switch has the same bug, so this fix fixes it there too. The one other web view that isn't covered is in OrcaSlicer's wipe-tower dialog, because it doesn't go through the shared creation code.

**1. Update check.**
- The accessor I added to OrcaSlicer's app class is reverted.
- Updates now shows only the JusPrin version and "JusPrin will look for newer versions itself in a later release."
- `known_update()` in `PreferencesWindow.cpp` is the placeholder JusPrin's own check will fill. It returns nothing for now, and the page already knows how to show a found update.
- I also removed "Stable releases only", since its only job was to configure OrcaSlicer's check.

**2. OrcaSlicer's files.** `Preferences.cpp/.hpp` are back to upstream. Instead of moving OrcaSlicer's code out, the window calls the same OrcaSlicer functions in place:
- **Dark mode:** the same four calls the dialog's checkbox makes, in the same order.
- **Language:** the same steps `open_preferences()` takes after its dialog closes.
- **Language list:** built from the translation files actually installed, each language named in its own language, instead of OrcaSlicer's hard-coded list.

What is left in OrcaSlicer's files, line by line:
- `GUI_App.hpp` +1: a private member holding the Preferences handler.
- `GUI_App.hpp` +3: a public `set_preferences_handler()` setter, with a two-line comment.
- `GUI_App.cpp` +2: at the top of `open_preferences()`, if a handler answers, return. Upstream's lines are untouched, so a rebase conflict here just means "keep both".
- `Widgets/WebView.cpp` +19 / −1: the language fix above (a constructor, a function that makes the settings, and one include). The one changed line is the one that creates the web view. Upstream could take this change as it is.

**3. New chats start with.** Each provider already has one built-in model, which is what new chats use: GPT-5.4 mini for OpenAI and OpenRouter, Claude Opus 5.5 for Anthropic. So the new Model row in Agent picks among the providers you have a key for, shown as "model · provider". It saves to the same setting setup uses for the default provider. With no key it says to add one first. I left out the Thinking row, because nothing stores a thinking level for new chats yet.

**4. Title bar: why the system one, and what I recommend.** With the system title bar you can drag the window aside to see the 3D view change behind it (units, theme, mouse settings). You also get the system's own close, Alt+F4 and dark title bar. A title row drawn by the web page can't be dragged unless we add separate native code for Windows, macOS and Linux. That is a real reason, so I've kept the system title bar for now. If Kenneth would rather match the canvas exactly, I can add that drag code.

**Checks:**
- The page's tests and type check pass.
- The AppConfig settings tests pass (14 cases), including the new-chat provider and the refusal of the removed update actions.
- In the running app (its own data folder), the theme switch with the in-place calls, the new Model row, and the three language switches all work.
